title: Rusting is a chemical change because it makes a new substance
summary: Rusting is a chemical change, because the rust is a different substance from the iron, oxygen, and water that were there before.
body: OpenStax Chemistry says a chemical change always produces one or more kinds of matter that differ from what was present before. Iron combining with oxygen in the presence of water to form rust is the example, and the page notes that chromium does not oxidize in the same way. Flammability, acidity, and reactivity are named as chemical properties, in contrast to physical ones such as density or hardness. Cooking, digestion, and rotting are also listed as chemical changes. This card is the rust example only. It does not say how fast a nail rusts outdoors.
